Subject: Feature-level economics & procurement — post-call next steps

Hi Samir / Procurement team,

Thanks again for a productive call earlier. Quick recap and the next actions we discussed so we can align internally at MediSys and at Redwood: 

Key outcomes from the call:
- You confirmed two feature bundles you want to pilot: "Clinical Triage Assistant" (high token per session) and "Clinical Summaries" (low token per session, higher session volume).
- Initial target for pilot window: 3 months, then evaluate expansion.
- Procurement asked for a simple cost model showing $/1M tokens, $/feature (per user or per session as appropriate), and an estimated CAC payback to justify the pilot spend.

What we need from you (action items):
1) Confirm monthly active sessions by feature (or typical sessions/day) for projected pilot cohorts — rough ranges are fine.
2) Indicate an internal procurement budget range for the pilot (ballpark min/max over the 3-month pilot).
3) Any compliance requirements that would materially affect hosting (VPC/on-prem or additional audit evidence).

Attached: Redwood-feature-econ-template.xlsx (simple worksheet we can fill with your numbers) and a one-page pilot-pricing-draft.pdf showing two sample pricing bands for a 3-month pilot.

Internal note: Priyom, can you draft a two-tiered breakdown showing (A) $/1M tokens baseline pricing and (B) per-feature cost estimates (tokens/session * $/token converted to $/feature)? Include a scenario for 100k sessions/month for Summaries and 10k sessions/month for Triage. Karthik, please review and flag any redlines for our finance team if the pilot discounts push margin below our target.

Next meeting: Samir suggested Wed next week to walk the procurement team through the worksheet — can we lock Wed 3pm PT?

Thanks,

Evelyn Hart
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood-feature-econ-template.xlsx (spreadsheet), pilot-pricing-draft.pdf (PDF)

Subject: RE: Feature-level economics & procurement — post-call next steps

Thanks Samir — that clarity helps a lot. I pulled together a quick set of scenarios (attached) and the highlights are below. I used conservative ops assumptions and our standard infra multipliers.

Summary of scenarios (3-month pilot aggregated):
- Baseline $/1M tokens (undiscounted public rate analog): $4,200 per 1M tokens (this is our internal reference price — not the offer).
- Scenario A (pilot standard discount): $2,800 / 1M tokens => Pilot cost @ 65.2M tokens/month ≈ $182.56k/month ⇒ $547.7k for 3 months (exceeds stated procurement cap).
- Scenario B (deeper pilot discount + commitment): $1,600 / 1M tokens => $104.32k/month ⇒ $312.96k for 3 months (still above max of $180k).
- Scenario C (feature-tiered approach):
   • Clinical Summaries: priced at $1,200 / 1M tokens (because lower latency and caching opportunities) => 40M tokens/month ⇒ $48k/month.
   • Clinical Triage: priced at $2,200 / 1M tokens (higher compute path) => 25.2M tokens/month ⇒ $55.44k/month.
   • Combined Scenario C cost ≈ $103.44k/month ⇒ $310.3k for 3 months.

Per-feature $/feature back-of-envelope (monthly):
- Summaries: tokens/session ≈ 400 => $/feature ≈ (400/1e6)*1,200 = $0.48 per session.
- Triage: tokens/session ≈ 1,400 => $/feature ≈ (1,400/1e6)*2,200 = $3.08 per session.

CAC payback note (assumptions):
- If MediSys captures $0.50 ARR per Summaries session and $3.50 ARR per Triage user/month, pilot economics look like: 
   • Summaries: gross margin per session ≈ $0.02 (bad) unless pricing or productization (batching/caching) reduces tokens.
   • Triage: gross margin per session ≈ $0.42 (better).
- For CAC payback we need to understand expected revenue uplift per pilot user and conversion to paying users post-trial. With current numbers, payback >12 months for Summaries unless we find more aggressive token reduction or a higher pricing plan.

Attachments: preliminary-scenarios.csv (small export), feature-tiered-pricing.pdf (visual).

Action items I propose:
1) Walk Samir + Procurement through Scenario C (feature-tiered) — this meets their mid pilot budget if we can secure a one-time pilot credit or commit to a timeline extension.
2) Redwood to provide a short list of optimizations: caching opportunities, quantized model variant for Triage, and a recommended batch/latency tradeoff.
3) Karthik to advise if we can offer an upfront pilot credit (one-time) that brings 3-month net spend into $180k range without hurting our target margins.

Priyom Das
Principal Product Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments: preliminary-scenarios.csv (CSV), feature-tiered-pricing.pdf (PDF)

Subject: Re: Feature-level economics & procurement — post-call next steps

Samir — appreciate the clear ranges. Quick summary from finance/ops perspective and a proposed path forward: 

1) Pilot offer (two-part):
   - Base usage pricing: feature-tiered as Priyom proposed (Summaries $1,200/1M, Triage $2,200/1M).
   - One-time pilot credit: Redwood can provide a $130k one-time credit applied across the 3-month pilot if MediSys signs a brief SOW committing to a technology evaluation and a 6-month post-pilot debrief. Credit reduces your net spend to ~ $180k in Scenario C.

2) Margin impact: accepting the credit reduces Redwood's short-term margin but preserves customer acquisition economics. Finance flags that sustained pricing must be higher to meet target gross margin (we should use pilot as a path to discuss volume tiers post-eval).

3) Contract & procurement documents: Evelyn — I attached a short SOW template and a DocuSign link we can use. Procurement team — please confirm required PO or SOW signatory.

Next step: I propose a 30-minute walkthrough Wed 3pm PT (same time) to go through the worksheet and the SOW. If that works, Evelyn please confirm and we’ll send a calendar invite and DocuSign to ProcureOps.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Pricing Strategy, Redwood Inference

Attachments: SOW-template.docx, DocuSign-link (sent separately)
